title: Alert
summary: Inline feedback with explicit severity text, appropriate live-region behavior, dismissal, and form-error guidance.
overview: A dependency-free inline feedback pattern that separates passive status from urgent alerts and never relies on color alone.

component.useWhen: Use an alert to explain the result of an action, a system condition, or a problem that needs attention near the affected content.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid alerts for neutral helper text, confirmations that need a blocking decision, or transient global notifications better handled by a toast.

examples.title: Feedback severities
examples.description: Compare informational, success, warning, and error messages, then dismiss any message with its labeled close control.

variants.title: Actionable alert
variants.summary: An inline message that offers a focused recovery action while retaining a labeled dismiss control.
variants.useWhen: Use an action when the alert can guide people directly to the next useful recovery step.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid stacking several competing actions inside one alert or using the action as a substitute for clear message text.
customization: Keep the action label specific to the recovery step and expose it as a native button.
The close control remains available for noncritical messages and uses the same alert:close event path.
Listen for alert:action to connect the button to the surrounding workflow.

example.title: Offer a recovery action
example.description: Use the action button to start the recommended recovery step, or dismiss the noncritical message.

variants.title: Minimal-size alert
variants.summary: A smaller alert treatment with tighter spacing for dense layouts while preserving severity and dismissal.
variants.useWhen: Use the minimal size when an alert must fit into a dense panel, toolbar, or compact form region.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid the minimal size for long explanations, urgent failures, or contexts where comfortable reading space is important.
customization: The minimal modifier reduces surface padding, gap, and supporting text scale without changing the alert semantics.
Keep the native dismiss button at the shared control size so it remains easy to target.
Use the normal size when the message needs more visual breathing room.

example.title: Minimal alert
example.description: Compare the compact surface with the normal alert size while keeping the same labeled dismiss behavior.

variants.title: Form error summary
variants.summary: An assertive error summary that links directly to invalid fields and complements inline error text.
variants.useWhen: Use an error summary after a failed form submission when several fields may need correction.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid announcing validation assertively on every keystroke; validate on blur or submission and preserve user input.
customization: Move focus to the summary only after submission when doing so helps users recover.
The summary link is disabled in this isolated preview to avoid navigating the host page; integrations can enable it when the field target is available.
Keep aria-invalid synchronized with the real validation state.

example.title: Validation summary
example.description: Follow the error link to the invalid email field and inspect the linked inline explanation.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: A nearby feedback surface with a status or alert role chosen by urgency.

anatomy.name: Severity cue
anatomy.description: A text label and symbol that communicate meaning without depending on color.

anatomy.name: Message
anatomy.description: Concise context and a recovery step when action is required.

anatomy.name: Dismiss control
anatomy.description: A labeled native button that removes a noncritical alert from layout and the accessibility tree.

accessibility: Use role=status for polite updates and role=alert only for urgent, newly introduced failures.
Include a visible severity label or meaningful wording; color and icons are supplementary.
Label close controls by the specific message they dismiss.
Link form summaries to fields and keep inline errors connected with aria-describedby.
Do not move focus for passive status updates.
component.responsive: Alerts fill their container and allow long text to wrap. Preview padding tightens below 32rem without shrinking controls.
limitations: Static messages already present at page load may not be announced as live updates in every screen reader.
The recipe does not manage a global message queue; use a toast region for transient application-wide notifications.

provenance.label: Cross-library message behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Badge
summary: A compact, noninteractive status or count label with inline, overlay, and dot-status patterns.
overview: A dependency-free badge for short metadata. It stays noninteractive, pairs color with text, and adds live-region behavior only when a changing value genuinely needs announcement.

component.useWhen: Use a badge to annotate another label or control with a short status, category, or count.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid badges for actions, long phrases, or critical feedback that needs an alert and recovery guidance.

examples.title: Inline statuses
examples.description: Compare neutral and emphasized status labels that communicate their meaning in text.

source.html: ApprovedIn reviewArchived

variants.title: Overlay count
variants.summary: A numeric badge positioned on a related control with a complete accessible name on the control.
variants.useWhen: Use an overlay count when the number directly annotates a familiar control such as an inbox.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid announcing rapidly changing counts unless each change requires immediate attention.
customization: The button accessible name contains the count, so the visual badge can be aria-hidden.
Keep the count short; use 99+ or a similarly understood cap for large values.
Reserve space around the target so the overlay is not clipped.

example.title: Inbox count
example.description: Focus the inbox control and confirm that its accessible name includes the unread count.

variants.title: Presence badge
variants.summary: A dot-and-text status label that remains understandable without color.
variants.useWhen: Use presence badges for a small set of stable availability states next to a person or service.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid implying exact availability from stale or unreliable presence data.
customization: Always retain the visible state text beside the dot.
Update dynamic presence politely only when the change matters in the current task.
Do not make the badge itself focusable unless it performs an action, in which case use a separate button.

example.title: Service presence
example.description: Read the explicit state labels; the dots are decorative reinforcements only.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: One or two words that state the category or status.

anatomy.name: Optional indicator
anatomy.description: A decorative dot or number that reinforces the text.

anatomy.name: Related target
anatomy.description: The nearby control or content the badge annotates.

accessibility: Keep badges noninteractive and out of the tab order.
State status in visible text instead of color alone.
When overlaying a control, include the count or state in the control's accessible name.
Use aria-live sparingly for dynamic values and avoid announcing decorative changes.
component.responsive: Inline badges wrap as a group and keep their content on one line; overlay badges remain anchored to their target.
limitations: Badges intentionally do not truncate long labels; authors should choose shorter language.
The overlay recipe assumes its target is not inside an overflow-clipped ancestor.

provenance.label: Cross-library badge behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Card
summary: A semantic content container with clear regions and a responsive horizontal layout.
overview: A dependency-free card that groups one coherent piece of content without inventing interaction semantics. Authors select article, section, or div according to the content.

component.useWhen: Use a card when a bounded content item benefits from a heading, supporting text, media, metadata, or actions.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid cards when ordinary headings and page sections already express the hierarchy, or when every surface becomes an unrelated box.

examples.title: Content card
examples.description: Inspect the article, labeled heading, supporting copy, and footer link as one self-contained item.

variants.title: Horizontal card
variants.summary: A media-and-content card that uses two columns when space allows and stacks naturally on narrow screens.
variants.useWhen: Use a horizontal card in wider lists where media helps identification and the text should remain compact.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid forcing a two-column card into a narrow sidebar or when the media is decorative noise.
customization: The media column is content-driven and the card switches to one column below 38rem.
Replace the CSS gradient with a local or product-provided asset; remote preview assets are intentionally excluded.
Keep the heading and primary link descriptive when cards appear in a repeated list.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: An article, section, or generic element selected for the content's real semantics.

anatomy.name: Optional media
anatomy.description: A visual preview that supports identification without replacing text.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.description: Heading and concise supporting content.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Metadata or a small number of related actions.

accessibility: Use article only when the card is independently meaningful; otherwise choose section or div.
Give repeated cards distinct headings and descriptive link text.
Do not add role=button or tabindex to a noninteractive card.
Keep source order logical when the horizontal layout collapses.
Avoid nested interactive controls inside a link that stretches over the entire card.
component.responsive: Cards cap their reading width. Horizontal cards switch from two columns to one below 38rem, preserving media-first source order.
limitations: The media treatment is a local CSS placeholder rather than a remote asset.
This recipe does not make the entire card clickable because doing so often creates nested-interaction and text-selection problems.

title: Progress bar
summary: A determinate or indeterminate task indicator with programmatic updates and reduced-motion behavior.
overview: A dependency-free progress indicator with explicit task labeling. Determinate progress exposes a real numeric value; indeterminate progress deliberately omits one.

component.useWhen: Use a progress bar for work that takes long enough for feedback to help people understand whether the task is advancing.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid progress bars for instant actions, decorative percentages, or unknown-duration work presented with a misleading numeric value.

examples.title: Determinate progress
examples.description: Set several completion values and inspect the synchronized visual width, text value, and aria-valuenow.

source.html: Uploading files40%

variants.title: Indeterminate progress
variants.summary: A labeled activity bar for work whose completion percentage cannot be calculated.
variants.useWhen: Use indeterminate progress when an operation is active but no honest completion estimate exists.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid leaving indeterminate progress onscreen without a task label, cancellation path, or eventual timeout handling.
customization: Omit aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax when the amount is unknown.
The animation becomes a static filled track under reduced-motion preferences.
Replace the status text when the task completes; hiding the bar alone can be ambiguous.

example.title: Unknown-duration import
example.description: Observe the activity indicator and test reduced-motion mode, where it becomes a static busy track.

anatomy.name: Task label
anatomy.description: Text identifying the operation being measured.

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.description: The total available progress range.

anatomy.name: Bar
anatomy.description: The completed proportion or an activity cue when indeterminate.

anatomy.name: Value text
anatomy.description: A visible value synchronized with aria-valuenow for determinate work.

accessibility: Label the progressbar with visible text using aria-labelledby.
Set aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuenow only when progress is determinate.
Keep visible percentage text synchronized with the programmatic value.
Respect reduced-motion preferences for indeterminate animation.
Announce completion in nearby status text when it is not otherwise obvious.
component.responsive: The track uses the full available width and the control row wraps on narrow screens.
limitations: The demo controls simulate application updates; production code must derive values from real work.
The indeterminate variant does not provide cancellation or timeout behavior.

provenance.label: Cross-library progress behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Skeleton
summary: A noninteractive loading placeholder for cards and lists with hidden status text and reduced-motion support.
overview: A dependency-free loading placeholder that mirrors the broad shape of incoming content without pretending to be usable content itself.

component.useWhen: Use a skeleton when the layout is known, content retrieval is noticeable, and preserving spatial stability improves the experience.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid skeletons for instant loads, unknown layouts, or operations where a labeled progress indicator provides more meaningful feedback.

examples.title: Card skeleton
examples.description: Inspect the placeholder as decorative content paired with a concise screen-reader status.

source.html: Loading project details.

variants.title: List skeleton
variants.summary: Repeated avatar-and-copy placeholders that preserve the expected dimensions of a loading list.
variants.useWhen: Use a list skeleton when the number and basic shape of rows are predictable before data arrives.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid rendering many placeholder rows; show only enough to establish the expected structure.
customization: Match placeholder count to the initial viewport rather than the full dataset.
Keep the entire placeholder list aria-hidden and announce loading once.
The avatar remains circular while text lengths vary to avoid a mechanical appearance.

example.description: Review three decorative placeholder rows and the single accessible loading announcement.

anatomy.name: Status
anatomy.description: One visually hidden live message describing what is loading.

anatomy.name: Placeholder group
anatomy.description: An aria-hidden shape approximation of the incoming layout.

anatomy.name: Shape
anatomy.description: A block representing media, a heading, copy, or an avatar.

accessibility: Hide decorative placeholder shapes from assistive technology.
Provide one concise role=status message for the loading region.
Remove or update the loading status when real content replaces the skeleton.
Disable pulse animation under prefers-reduced-motion.
Never make skeleton shapes focusable or interactive.
component.responsive: Skeleton groups fill their container up to a readable maximum width and preserve their internal proportions on narrow screens.
limitations: Skeletons do not communicate measurable progress.
The example does not perform data loading or replacement; the consumer owns that lifecycle.

provenance.label: Cross-library skeleton behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Breadcrumb
summary: A semantic location trail with horizontal overflow and a native collapsed-middle variant.
overview: A dependency-free breadcrumb that identifies the current page with aria-current and keeps navigation semantics separate from interactive tabs or step progress.

component.useWhen: Use breadcrumbs in a hierarchical site or application where people may need to move to an ancestor level.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid them for shallow structures, browsing history, workflow steps, or a list of sibling filters.

examples.title: Location trail
examples.description: Follow ancestor links and inspect the final non-link item marked as the current page.

variants.title: Collapsed middle
variants.summary: A long hierarchy whose intermediate ancestors are available from a native details disclosure.
variants.useWhen: Use a collapsed middle when a deep hierarchy would otherwise dominate a narrow header.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid hiding the immediate parent or the current page, which are usually the most useful orientation cues.
customization: Keep Home, the immediate parent, and current page visible.
The details summary has a descriptive accessible label rather than only an ellipsis.
The popup contains ordinary links and closes with the native details behavior.

example.description: Open the middle-level disclosure to reach hidden ancestors while the root, parent, and current page remain visible.

anatomy.name: Navigation landmark
anatomy.description: A nav labeled Breadcrumb.

anatomy.name: Ordered trail
anatomy.description: Ancestor locations in hierarchy order.

anatomy.name: Ancestor link
anatomy.description: A navigable parent level.

anatomy.name: Current page
anatomy.description: A non-link final item marked with aria-current=page.

accessibility: Wrap the trail in a labeled navigation landmark.
Use an ordered list to preserve hierarchy.
Mark the final item with aria-current=page and do not link it to itself.
Keep link text concise and unique enough in context.
Allow horizontal overflow rather than shrinking targets or clipping text.
component.responsive: The default trail scrolls horizontally within its own surface. The collapsed variant reduces deep middle levels while retaining orientation anchors.
limitations: The collapsed details popup uses simple static positioning and does not perform viewport collision detection.
Breadcrumbs represent information architecture, not the user's chronological browser history.
